description: Machine-readable expected outcome for every fixture in this directory. `verify-fixtures.mjs` reads this file and fails (non-zero exit) if any fixture's actual outcome does not match. Each entry's `type` selects which check applies: "record" (a single decision/v1 record, checked against the schema, the personal-dimension scan, the within-record retractions<->decision_items consistency check, and contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs's byte-level digest check) or "collection" (an array of records checked together, the only way to express the conflicts_with cross-record dangling-reference check -- same convention release-observation/v0 uses for its own rollback_of check). `reason_code` for a "reject" fixture is either a named semantic-check code or a raw schema-validator JSON-path, same leading-token convention as this repo's other contracts. PROVENANCE: the four individual accept records (decision-01 through decision-04) are drawn from the one real I-shadow case this repo has recorded -- `docs/protocols/i-shadow-record-01-living-twin-2026-08-17.md` and the living-twin repo's own `docs/decisions/decision-01-pivot-and-scope-2026-08-17.md`, `decision-02-thresholds-2026-08-17.md`, `decision-03-discovery-scope-2026-08-17.md`, and `decision-04-two-stage-discovery-2026-08-17.md` (none of these source files ship in this repo; they are an external, private working repo -- notes here cite them for provenance without vendoring them). `evidence_snapshot_digest` on each of the four is a real `sha256sum` of an actual source markdown file this task independently recomputed (decision-01 -> the LUNAR-existence correction that grounds its rationale; decision-02, decision-03, decision-04 -> each decision's own source file). `options_ref` (per its own field description: 'the design-options/v1 document ... resolved against') carries `uri` + real `sha256sum` of THIS repo's own `contracts/design-options/v1/fixtures/accept-living-twin-*.json` file (no `source_repo` -- same repo), recomputed after those files were finalized (see M10/circular-dependency note in docs/protocols/decision-v1.md: editing a design-options fixture invalidates every decision fixture's `options_ref.content_digest` that points at it, so design-options/v1 must be finalized first). `critic_ref` carries `uri` + `source_repo: "living-twin"` + real `sha256sum` of the actual living-twin critic file (`independent-review-diff-2026-08-17.md` / `terra-independent-threshold-derivation.txt` / `sol-round2-self-attack.txt`, the last shared correctly by decision-03 and decision-04 since both cite the same critic pass) -- unverifiable in CI by design (living-twin is external, unvendored), reported as such, never silently accepted. `logical_id` on `critic_ref` is `living-twin:<source-basename-without-extension>`, distinct per real file, so it can never again collide with `options_ref`'s own logical_id the way an earlier version of these fixtures did (see 'Known review findings, corrected' below). `intent_ref` is uniform across all four (`living-twin:user-authored-investigation-brief-prose`, `digest_omitted_reason` set, text unchanged) -- the real case's intent was the same prose brief for every one of these four decisions, not a per-decision document. decision-03's own rationale field is deliberately candid about a real mismatch in the source material: decision-03's text names its selection "選択肢C" but the design actually frozen there is a hybrid, not an exact match for decision-03-input's original catalogued option C -- this fixture records that mismatch rather than silently reconciling it (see docs/protocols/decision-v1.md's own 'Known source-material inconsistency' note). The accept-conflict-resolves-collection fixture reuses decision-03 and decision-04 verbatim to demonstrate conflicts_with resolving correctly across a real collection (decision-04's own conflicts_with really does point at decision-03's real decision_id). The two demo-decision-* records and the two dangling-conflicting-decision-ref-collection-*.json files are the one exception: clearly-labeled synthetic minimal records, invented because no real recorded decision in this case exhibits a dangling conflicts_with reference -- mirroring release-observation/v0's own synthetic demo-release@* precedent for the same reason. KNOWN REVIEW FINDINGS, CORRECTED (kept here rather than erased, per this repo's own no-silent-reconciliation norm applied to its own fixture history): an earlier version of these four fixtures gave `options_ref` and `critic_ref` the SAME `logical_id` despite pointing at different real documents, and gave `intent_ref` a `content_digest` for a document that was never filed at all (no `uri` field existed to record what any digest was even for) -- all seven underlying digest VALUES were real sha256sums of real files throughout, just attached to the wrong logical_id / missing the uri needed to check them, which is why a reviewer without `uri` to go on had to brute-force-hash an external repo to guess what they meant, and briefly misattributed one in the process. See docs/protocols/decision-v1.md's own account of this incident for the full timeline.

fixtures.notes: living-twin decision-01-pivot-and-scope-2026-08-17.md in full: Pivot/Discovery GO selected over the unmodified original plan, Kill, and the alternative AI-Social/companion pivot. no_action_option_id names "kill" (a genuinely framed do-nothing option in this case). status=active, retractions=[] (this decision was never partially retracted).

living-twin decision-02-thresholds-2026-08-17.md: terra's independently-derived thresholds selected over sol's. Exercises the partial-retraction machinery this contract's own decision_items[]/retractions[] pair exists for (i-shadow-record-01 'finding 1'): the Barnum threshold sub-item is individually retracted via the decision's own 追記v2, while the rest of the decision (main-trial-threshold, import-completion-threshold, sample-bias-handling) stays active -- exactly the fact D10's document-level status(active|superseded) alone cannot express. no_action_option_id is null (this decision never framed a distinct 'freeze no thresholds' alternative), paired with a required no_action_rationale quoting why.

living-twin decision-03-discovery-scope-2026-08-17.md. status=superseded, superseded_by points at decision-04 (checked as individually schema-valid here -- only the collection fixture below cross-checks that the reference actually resolves).

living-twin decision-04-two-stage-discovery-2026-08-17.md: the real recorded conflict (i-shadow-record-01 section 2(c), called the single most important finding). conflicts_with names decision-03 as the conflicting decision and "tertiary-phase-direct-instruction" as the OTHER channel -- a channel that, per the real case, never produced its own citable decision/v1 record at all (this schema's own conflict.conflicting_channel_id description explains why that is allowed). no_action_option_id is null: this decision arose from reconciling a channel conflict, not a fresh design-options round, so no do-nothing option was ever framed for it.

The same decision-03/decision-04 pair, checked together: decision-04's conflicts_with[0].conflicting_decision_ref.logical_id ("living-twin-decision-03-discovery-scope") DOES resolve to decision-03's own decision_id within this two-record collection -- the positive case for the cross-record check, using real (not synthetic) data, unlike the dangling-reference fixture below.

All 11 forbidden personal-dimension keys planted at once (as extra top-level properties) on top of accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json. Also independently caught 11 times over by additionalProperties:false (this schema's top level is fully closed).

decision_channel is omitted entirely from accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json -- the field i-shadow-record-01 section 2(c) calls the single most important addition this contract makes over D10. Caught by the schema's top-level `required` list.

accept-living-twin-decision-03-discovery-scope.json with `superseded_by` deleted while `status` stays "superseded" -- the exact failure mode named in this task's own invalid-fixture requirements. Caught by the schema's conditional `required` (allOf if/then on status=="superseded").

accept-living-twin-decision-02-thresholds.json with retractions[0].retracted_item_ref changed to "item-that-does-not-exist", which matches no decision_items[].item_id in this record -- the exact failure mode named in this task's own invalid-fixture requirements ("retraction が存在しない項目を指す"). Individually schema-valid (a plain non-empty string); only the semantic check in verify-fixtures.mjs catches it.

accept-living-twin-decision-02-thresholds.json with the barnum-threshold-gate decision_items[] entry's status changed back to "active" while retractions[] still claims it was retracted -- the inconsistent-but-not-dangling half of the same check. A real retraction always flips the item's own status; this fixture proves the check catches the case where that link is broken instead of merely missing.

Two synthetic (clearly non-real, demo-decision-*) records: demo-decision-2's conflicts_with[0].conflicting_decision_ref points at "demo-decision-999", a decision_id that appears nowhere in this collection. Invented rather than sourced from real data because no real recorded decision in this case exhibits a dangling conflicts_with reference -- mirroring release-observation/v0's own synthetic dangling-rollback-of-collection fixture for the identical reason.

accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json with the last hex digit of options_ref.content_digest flipped (...744 -> ...745), so it no longer matches the real sha256 of contracts/design-options/v1/fixtures/accept-living-twin-pivot-options.json that options_ref.uri actually points at (a real, same-repo file -- no separate synthetic self-referential fixture is needed for this once options_ref resolves inside this repo by construction). Individually schema-valid (still matches ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, the only thing schema validation alone can ever check about a digest) -- only contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs's actual byte-level check catches it. This is the exact incident (sol architect-review must-fix 1) the artifact_ref/decision_ref split and this digest-verification module exist to close: a formally-valid content_digest that does not match the file it claims to. (An earlier version of this fixture used a synthetic demo record pointing at LICENSE/contracts/shared/*.mjs instead -- no longer necessary now that a real accept fixture's own options_ref is repo-internal and verifiable.)

accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json with critic_ref's uri (and source_repo) deleted while content_digest stays. Caught by $defs/artifact_ref's new content_digest-present-implies-uri-required conditional -- added specifically because the earlier lack of `uri` on these very refs was what let a reviewer misattribute a digest by brute-force hashing (see this directory's own top-level PROVENANCE note). Also independently re-checked by contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs's own standalone artifact_ref_digest_without_uri check, so the module still catches this even when used outside full schema validation.

accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json with critic_ref.logical_id changed to be identical to options_ref.logical_id, while each ref keeps its own distinct, individually-correct uri/content_digest (both real, both verifiable, both actually different files). Individually schema-valid (logical_id has no cross-field uniqueness constraint at the schema level) -- only contracts/shared/verify-artifact-digests.mjs's cross-ref check catches it. This is deliberately the mirror image of the fabricated-digest incident: an identifier reused across two refs that provably resolve to different real content, the exact shape an earlier version of these four accept fixtures had before this task's correction (see this directory's own top-level PROVENANCE note).

accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json with estimate_refs_omitted_reason deleted while estimate_refs stays []. Caught by the schema's top-level conditional `required` (allOf if/then on estimate_refs.maxItems==0) -- the null-not-zero rule this field exists to enforce (i-shadow-record-01 section 4, 'finding 3') previously had no reject fixture proving it actually fires.

accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json with options_ref carrying BOTH content_digest (already present) AND a synthetic digest_omitted_reason. Exercises $defs/artifact_ref's mutual-exclusion conditional (sol architect-review must-fix 2): 'here is the digest' and 'the digest is missing because X' cannot both be true of the same ref at once. This is the specific gap the pre-split $defs/ref left open -- a producer could truthfully claim both.

accept-living-twin-decision-01-pivot.json with options_ref's content_digest deleted, leaving only logical_id (no digest_omitted_reason either). Caught by $defs/artifact_ref's existing null-not-zero conditional (content_digest absent -> digest_omitted_reason required) -- an artifact_ref that says neither 'here is the digest' nor 'here is why there isn't one' is exactly the silent gap this contract does not allow.

accept-living-twin-decision-03-discovery-scope.json with a synthetic content_digest added to superseded_by. Caught by $defs/decision_ref's additionalProperties:false (sol architect-review must-fix 3): a ledger-internal reference to another decision/v1 record is resolved by logical_id alone and deliberately carries no digest field at all, so this is rejected as an unknown property, not merely an unverifiable one.
